checkpoint_review: The Router correctly identified that the posterior back (dorsal knuckles), baleen plates, flippers, and tail flukes are not visible due to the breaching pose and water occlusion. Marking these as 'is_testable: false' is accurate; penalizing the image for missing features that are physically impossible to see in this specific frame would be incorrect. The Router was also correct to mark the head shape and skin texture as present. I agree with all Router verdicts regarding testability and presence.
artifact_review: The Router identified a texture anomaly (painted-on barnacles) and structural collapse at the water interface. I agree with the severity of the water interface issue (2.0); the splash lacks physical coherence and merges unnaturally with the whale's body, a common AI failure mode in fluid dynamics. The texture anomaly (1.5) is also valid; the white speckles lack distinct 3D relief and appear flat. Additionally, the perceptual_quality_auditor detected moderate compression artifacts (score 0.4), which manifests as slight pixelation/blockiness in the water and sky. This adds to the artifact burden. The topology_boundary_auditor gave a high confidence score (0.99), but this likely reflects the model's ability to segment the high-contrast subject rather than confirming physical realism of the boundary, so the Router's observation of 'melting' takes precedence over the expert's segmentation confidence.
alignment_reasoning: All visible checkpoints (head shape, skin mottling, robust body, rough texture) are correctly rendered. The fine-grained classifier confirmed 'grey whale' with high confidence (logit 7.94). Unseen features were correctly marked N/A. No anatomical errors in visible regions.
artifact_reasoning: Router correctly flagged water-body fusion (severity 2.0) and flat barnacle texture (severity 1.5). Expert auditor added moderate compression artifacts (0.4). Total artifact load is significant enough to prevent a top-tier score but does not constitute catastrophic failure.
